task.description:
RELEASE-VALIDATOR pass (WF-02 Step 5) for REQ-168 (queue task 320, GH#620). Independently re-derive that every one of REQ-168's real acceptance criteria in docs/requirements.yaml is genuinely met -- do not trust any prior step's self-report, re-run and re-check yourself. All prior gates (design, security, reviewer, test-design-validator, test-runner) have passed; your job is the final independent cross-check before DOC-UPDATER marks it done. Use export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" and WASMEX_BUILD=true for wasmex-touching commands.

SAFETY REMINDER: memory_guard_test.exs is designed so that no test ever calls a live Wasmex.Memory function with a magnitude >= 2^40 (independently verified by 3 prior gates already, given a real live-confirmed SIGABRT hazard at that magnitude). Do not write any ad hoc verification script that violates this constraint.
acceptance_criteria: Re-read REQ-168's full entry in docs/requirements.yaml and independently map each real AC to the shipped code (lib/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard.ex) and its tests -- do not just re-read prior handoffs' claims.
Re-run mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/ yourself, quote real output.
Re-run mix compile --warnings-as-errors yourself, quote real output.
Re-run the AC1 repo-search yourself: grep -rn 'Wasmex.Memory\.' lib/ --include='*.ex' and confirm hits are confined to memory_guard.ex.

Confirm no scope creep beyond what REQ-168 authorized (cross-check git diff --stat main...HEAD against owned_modules) -- module_registry.ex, capability_gate.ex, plugin_handler.ex, and application.ex must be untouched.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-168 (lib/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard.ex, commit 69f021e). All 6 real acceptance_criteria in docs/requirements.yaml (lines 8547-8553) confirmed against shipped code/tests, not prior handoffs' claims.
acceptance_criteria_findings: AC1 (single validation function + repo-search): check_bounds/3 is the sole arithmetic core; read/4 and write/4 are the only functions that ever call Wasmex.Memory.*. Re-ran `grep -rn 'Wasmex.Memory\.' lib/ --include='*.ex'` myself -- all 10 hits are inside lib/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard.ex (comments referencing Wasmex.Memory.size/2/read_binary/write_binary plus the 4 real call sites at lines 132,136,156,161). No other file in lib/ references Wasmex.Memory. PASS.

AC2 (malformed pointer -> structured error, BEAM node stays up): test/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard_test.exs describe "T3 (AC2)" -- 4 live tests build a real Wasmex instance, pass a malformed offset/length to read/4 and write/4, assert the {:error, {:invalid_pointer, ...}} tuple, then assert Process.alive?(self()) and Process.whereis(Letflow.Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor) |> Process.alive?(). All 4 passed in my own re-run. PASS.

AC3 (offset-beyond-size, length-past-end, offset+length overflow, each rejected pre-dereference): describe "T2 (AC3)" covers all three shapes purely via check_bounds/3 (no live Wasmex call for the extreme-magnitude cases, per the SIGABRT safety constraint -- verified no test in the file calls read/4, write/4, or any live Wasmex.Memory function with a value >= 2^40; the 2^63/2^64-magnitude cases target check_bounds/3 only). PASS.

AC4 (per-instance isolation): describe "T4 (AC4)" starts two real Wasmex instances, writes into instance A, asserts instance B still reads the original zero byte and A retains its write. Passed in my re-run. PASS.

AC5 (moduledoc discloses the Wasmtime-native residual class, consistent with REQ-165): moduledoc (memory_guard.ex lines 2-46) states 'does NOT bound a fault occurring inside Wasmtime's own native code/runtime itself', cites req165-wasmex-process-boundary.md sec 7.2 by name, and quotes its 'does not raise, exit, or trap in the ordinary BEAM sense' text verbatim. describe "T5 (AC5)" tests this via Code.fetch_docs/1 and both passed. PASS.
AC6 (mix test / mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass, real output quoted): re-ran both myself, see raw_command_output below. PASS.

result.safety_constraint_check: Re-read memory_guard_test.exs in full: confirmed no test calls a live Wasmex.Memory function (via read/4, write/4, or directly) with a magnitude >= 2^40. The two extreme-magnitude tests (2^63, 2^64) call check_bounds/3 only, which is pure Elixir bignum arithmetic with zero Wasmex/NIF dependency. Did not write or run any ad hoc verification script that would violate this constraint.
result.verdict: REQ-168 acceptance criteria are genuinely met by the shipped code and tests as of commit 69f021e on feature/WF02-REQ168-20260828. No discrepancy found between prior gates' self-reports and independently re-derived reality. Cleared for DOC-UPDATER.
